entities.summary: Gedrosia is the Hellenized name of the part of coastal Makran in what is now Balochistan. In the accounts about Alexander the Great and his successors, the area referred to as Gedrosia runs from the Indus River to the north-eastern edge of the Strait of Hormuz. It is directly to the south of the provinces of Arachosia and Drangiana, to the east of the province of Carmania, and due west of the Indus which formed a natural boundary between it and western India. The native name of Gedrosia might have been Gwadar or Gwatar as there are two towns by that name and three bays with similar names in central Makran.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gedrosia's geographical boundaries and cultural significance influenced the ancient trade routes between India and the Mediterranean, with the Indus River serving as a major border. The area played a crucial role in the Hellenistic conquests of Alexander the Great.
